# Modern Perl Patterns

Curated by Skill Harbor: a modernization guide that makes Muse write and review Perl 5.36+ the way current Perl developers do, not the way Perl looked in 2005. It starts with the single use v5.36 pragma that replaces the old strict/warnings boilerplate and enables signatures, then covers subroutine signatures with defaults and slurpy parameters, scalar versus list context, postfix dereferencing for readable nested structures, and the infix isa operator. Error handling moves from eval/die to Try::Tiny and the native try/catch of 5.40+. Modern OO prefers Moo with typed attributes and roles over blessed hashrefs, with the native class keyword of 5.38+ as the coming standard. Regular expressions get named captures with the /x flag and precompiled qr// patterns. File I/O uses three-argument open with autodie and Path::Tiny, module organization follows a standard lib/bin/t layout with Exporter, and the tooling section covers perltidy, perlcritic and cpanfile with carton. A legacy-to-modern quick reference table and an anti-pattern list (two-arg open, string eval, no strict refs) close the skill. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: the modern features need Perl 5.36 or newer, check your production version before adopting; the native class keyword is still experimental in some versions; it will not make legacy CPAN code disappear. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
